plan.raw_excerpt:
External plan review, mode=iterate, provider=openrouter (2 of 2 reached).
Verdicts: gemini=approve, openai=revise. Contradiction: none (agree within one step).

openai HIGH x3:
 1 dependency — a new tool plus prose wires nothing; exit 6 needs a handler in every caller.
 2 approach  — "no rulesets" is not evidence auto-merge is impossible; classic branch
   protection answers [] while arming works. Limit `unavailable` to definitive conditions.
 3 edge-case — race on PR head AND base between verification and merge; pin the head SHA
   and use the host's conditional-head merge.
openai MED x4: 4 BEHIND/UNKNOWN/post-push settling unmapped; 5 default-on self-merge widens
 token authority, validate PR identity + fail closed on a bad switch value; 6 reuse the
 watcher's rollup logic instead of re-implementing, prove ready_is_terminal=False unchanged;
 7 clip() TRUNCATES at 120 chars — comparing clipped values would accept two distinct long ids.
gemini MED x2 / LOW x2: transient UNKNOWN mergeability; base advances during verification;
 pass --run-id through to re-verification; draft-PR arm failure must classify as transient.

Disposition: ALL eleven folded into the plan; none declined. Two changed the design shape —
`protected` (readable without admin, covers rulesets AND classic) replaced the rulesets
discriminator, and a non-truncating canonical_run_id was split from the display clip().
Full table: iterate spec section 6.

findings.finding: The 'checks do not vanish' floor was a COUNT starting at 0, so (a) the first poll merged an empty-but-CLEAN rollup before Actions had created its check runs, and (b) three checks reporting where three were seen before passed even when the refreshed base had grown to five.
Three test files crossed the 300-line source limit with no baseline entry, which the Group H audit fails HIGH after merge.
readiness fell through to GREEN for any unrecognised mergeStateStatus, so a new enum member would license a merge on no evidence.
DIRTY was bucketed with BLOCKED, so a branch that conflicted after another iterate merged polled to the 1800s timeout even though ensure_current is the remedy and is already wired into this ladder.
The pin guaranteed less than it read: --match-head-commit pins whatever the PR head IS, so a commit pushed by anyone else during the wait would have been pinned and merged unverified.
The pre-merge re-read ran a PR merged in the meantime through the OPEN-only identity check and returned a REFUSAL, aborting the iterate over a PR that was merged and green.

No subprocess call had a timeout. timeout_seconds bounds the polling clock, which is consulted only AFTER a fetch returns, so a hung gh escaped every stated bound and the run neither delivered nor failed.

'Never raises' was false: a missing gh is an OSError, a blank-stdout zero exit a JSONDecodeError, a null rollup entry an AttributeError — all escaped the except RuntimeError sites as tracebacks instead of the documented exit 5.

--repo was omitted on every mutating call while the watcher passed it, and identity compared branch NAMES only — so a fork and its upstream both matched and the arm could act on one repository while the watch watched another.
timeout_seconds was spent per attempt, silently making --timeout-seconds 1800 a 5400-second block.
Six loose host callables whose defaults disagreed: capability closed over the MODULE-level gh_json, so faking gh_json alone still fired real gh api calls at the operator's live GitHub.

The campaign predicate had two readers of one switch; the structural-marker comment claimed a gating the code did not do; render_pair blamed truncation for every collision; the invisible class was missing SOFT HYPHEN, WORD JOINER, BOM and the grapheme joiner; two assertions could not fail; the composition harness would HANG rather than fail on a non-terminating implementation; one ledger citation named a test that no longer existed.
"Never trust the exit code alone — re-read the state"
"the head is also compared with the local HEAD this run verified"
"What merges is what was verified"
"step 0: is this PR even ours? Before anything mutating"
"the refresh happens immediately before it"
"Case B needs no branch of its own ... the host refuses our merge if they are unmet"
The merge is a remote-only operation
"how many checks the host actually ran"
"The wall-clock budget is spent ONCE across all attempts"
no false-PASS in canonical_run_id
a refusal names the right cause

external_code.raw_excerpt:
External CODE review, mode=code, provider=openrouter.
Verdicts: openai=revise (5 findings), gemini=DEGRADED (reply truncated by the provider at
finish_reason=length — its visible portion raised the same Host.default binding point as
openai's, and is treated as a real finding rather than discarded).

openai HIGH x2:
 1 spec — an arm failure with allow_auto_merge=False and base_protected=True classifies
   ARM_SETTING_OFF (exit 6) while the spec's own case table still promised a self-merge
   fallback for case B. A genuine code-vs-spec divergence.
   DISPOSITION: the CODE is right and the SPEC was stale. The narrowing came from Stage 3
   (a protected base carries required reviews an operator-token merge may bypass, and the
   remedy is one checkbox), and F11.md/guide.md/hooks-and-pipeline.md had already been
   updated — section 2's case table had not. Spec corrected; the narrowing stands and is
   surfaced to the operator in the run summary.
 2 security — the structural-marker path returned ARM_UNAVAILABLE even when BOTH facts read
   permissively, so an error STRING alone could route a PROTECTED PR into self-merge. That
   is precisely the hole the Stage-3 narrowing exists to close.
   DISPOSITION: FIXED. A marker match can no longer promote past `base_protected is True`;
   there it yields ARM_SETTING_OFF (report, do not merge). Case C still works when only one
   fact is readable, because the marker itself asserts the base has no protection.
   Tests: test_pr_delivery::test_permissive_facts_plus_a_structural_marker_stays_blocked_on_a_protected_base,
   ::test_a_structural_marker_still_carries_an_unprotected_or_unreadable_base.

openai MEDIUM x3:
 3 bug — head_before was read AFTER ensure_current ran, so the unparseable-guard comparison
   could never detect the commit it exists to detect. FIXED (read before), and the test
   helper's call ordering was corrected with it.
 4 bug — the successful self-merge result dropped the watch verdict's checks_passed, so
   summary() fell back to the observed count and called every observed check "passing",
   re-opening the Stage-3 skipped-is-not-evidence finding. FIXED: checks_passed is carried
   through the loop and into the delivered result.
 5 test — no test asserted "permissive facts + arm failure => blocked" or the protected-base
   fallback. FIXED by the two tests named under finding 2, plus
   test_auto_merge_off_on_a_PROTECTED_base_is_not_self_merge_eligible and the integration
   test test_a_protected_base_whose_setting_is_off_is_reported_not_merged.

gemini (degraded/truncated) — Host.default() aliased the module-level functions rather than
BINDING capability to the bundle's own gh_json, so the docstring's guarantee depended on
every call site remembering `reader=host.gh_json`. FIXED with functools.partial, so the
binding is a property of the factory and cannot be forgotten.

Nothing was declined. Two findings changed behaviour (the marker/protected interaction and
the checks_passed carry-through); one corrected the spec rather than the code, explicitly.
